# The sequencing run and its correction Cre mice were sequenced only in 2025-10; most GFP controls only in 2025-04. This chapter measures the run difference with the bridge mice, fits the main model with a batch term, and benchmarks the alternatives. ## Technical differences between runs Ribosomal-protein and mitochondrial read fractions are technical readouts of RNA extraction / library prep. If they track extraction batch rather than treatment, any "translation / OXPHOS" signal in a model without batch is an artifact. Batch is therefore in the design (`design_for()`). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ribo_rx <- "^Rp[ls]\\d+[a-z]?\\d*$|^Rplp\\d$|^Rpsa$" sym <- id2name$Symbol[match(rownames(geneCounts), id2name$ensemblID)] lib <- colSums(geneCounts) tech <- tibble(sample = colnames(geneCounts), pct_ribosomal_protein = 100 * colSums(geneCounts[str_detect(replace_na(sym, ""), ribo_rx) %in% TRUE, ]) / lib, pct_mitochondrial = 100 * colSums(geneCounts[str_detect(replace_na(sym, ""), "^mt-") %in% TRUE, ]) / lib) |> left_join(rownames_to_column(meta, "sample"), by = "sample") |> dplyr::filter(arm == "AAV") write_csv(tech, file.path(CSV_DIR, "qc", "technical_fractions_by_batch.csv")) # treatment x batch layout per tissue dplyr::count(tech, tissue, treatment, .data[[BATCH]]) |> pivot_wider(names_from = all_of(BATCH), values_from = n, values_fill = 0, names_prefix = "batch_") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # correlation of each fraction with treatment and with batch tech |> pivot_longer(starts_with("pct_"), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |> group_by(tissue, metric) |> # variance explained (R^2) by each factor alone; batch has 3 levels, so R^2 rather than r summarise(r2_treatment = summary(lm(value ~ treatment))$r.squared, r2_batch = summary(lm(value ~ .data[[BATCH]]))$r.squared, r2_rin = summary(lm(value ~ rin))$r.squared, .groups = "drop") # basis for USE_RIN ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} p_tech <- tech |> pivot_longer(starts_with("pct_"), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |> mutate(metric = recode(metric, pct_ribosomal_protein = "Ribosomal protein reads (%)", pct_mitochondrial = "Mitochondrial reads (%)"), batch = paste("Batch", .data[[BATCH]])) |> ggplot(aes(batch, value, colour = treatment)) + geom_point(size = 1.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) + facet_grid(metric ~ tissue, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") + scale_colour_manual(values = GROUP_COLS) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_bulk() + theme(strip.placement = "outside", legend.position = "right") save_plot(p_tech, file.path(FIG_DIR, "qc", "technical_fractions_by_batch"), "full", 75) p_tech ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-run-correction_files/figure-html/technical-check-1.png){width=643.2} ::: ::: ## Bridge mice: the same animals in both runs SAD_326 and MAD_271 were sequenced in both runs. The same tissue from the same mouse should differ only technically, so the 2025-04 vs 2025-10 difference for these pairs is the run effect. It is compared with the spread between *different* GFP mice within the 2025-04 run, and the APOE genotype calls are lined up to confirm each pair is the same animal. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} bridge <- meta |> rownames_to_column("sample") |> dplyr::filter(arm == "AAV", treatment == "GFP") |> group_by(tissue, mouse_id) |> dplyr::filter(n_distinct(run) == 2) |> ungroup() if (nrow(bridge) == 0) { message("No bridge pairs counted yet") } else { logcpm_tissue <- function(tissue) { cts <- geneCounts[gene_qc[[tissue]]$keep, , drop = FALSE] log2(t(t(cts) / colSums(cts) * 1e6) + 1) } lc <- map(set_names(TISSUES), logcpm_tissue) # bridge pairs: same mouse, two runs pair_stats <- bridge |> dplyr::select(tissue, mouse_id, run, sample) |> pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = sample) |> mutate(type = "same mouse, 2025-04 vs 2025-10", r = pmap_dbl(list(tissue, `2025-04`, `2025-10`), \(t, a, b) cor(lc[[t]][, a], lc[[t]][, b])), n_genes_2fold = pmap_int(list(tissue, `2025-04`, `2025-10`), \(t, a, b) sum(abs(lc[[t]][, a] - lc[[t]][, b]) > 1))) # reference: different GFP mice within the 2025-04 run ref_stats <- map(TISSUES, \(t) { s <- rownames(meta)[meta$tissue == t & meta$treatment == "GFP" & meta$run == "2025-04"] combn(s, 2, simplify = FALSE) |> map(\(p) tibble(tissue = t, a = p[1], b = p[2], r = cor(lc[[t]][, p[1]], lc[[t]][, p[2]]), n_genes_2fold = sum(abs(lc[[t]][, p[1]] - lc[[t]][, p[2]]) > 1))) }) |> bind_rows() |> mutate(type = "different mice, 2025-04") bridge_summary <- bind_rows( dplyr::select(pair_stats, tissue, type, mouse_id, r, n_genes_2fold), ref_stats |> group_by(tissue, type) |> summarise(mouse_id = "median of all pairs", r = median(r), n_genes_2fold = as.integer(median(n_genes_2fold)), .groups = "drop")) write_csv(bridge_summary, file.path(CSV_DIR, "qc", "bridge_replicate_check.csv")) print(bridge_summary) geno_file <- file.path(IN_DIR, "mcc_results", "apoe_transgene_check", "apoe_genotype_calls.tsv") if (file.exists(geno_file)) read_tsv(geno_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |> dplyr::filter(sample %in% bridge$sample) |> left_join(dplyr::select(bridge, sample, mouse_id, tissue, run), by = "sample") |> arrange(tissue, mouse_id, run) |> print() p_bridge <- pmap(dplyr::select(pair_stats, tissue, mouse_id, `2025-04`, `2025-10`, r), \(tissue, mouse_id, `2025-04`, `2025-10`, r) ggplot(tibble(x = lc[[tissue]][, `2025-04`], y = lc[[tissue]][, `2025-10`]), aes(x, y)) + geom_point(size = 0.2, alpha = 0.3, stroke = 0) + geom_abline(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#C51B7D") + labs(title = sprintf("%s · %s (r = %.3f)", tissue, mouse_id, r), x = "2025-04 log2(CPM + 1)", y = "2025-10 log2(CPM + 1)") + theme_bulk()) |> wrap_plots(ncol = 2) save_plot(p_bridge, file.path(FIG_DIR, "qc", "bridge_replicates"), "full", 120) p_bridge } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # ℹ 1 more variable: run ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-run-correction_files/figure-html/bridge-check-1.png){width=643.2} ::: ::: ## DESeq2 model: Cre vs GFP with a batch term ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # AAV samples of a tissue. dedup = TRUE (every model): ONE sample per mouse. MAD_271 and SAD_326 # were sequenced in both runs (the same animals, not separate controls), so their 2025-04 copy is # dropped wherever a usable 2025-10 copy exists; the 2025-10 copy is kept because it anchors the # batch term against the 2025-10 Cre mice. (SAD_326 brain: its 2025-10 sample B13 is excluded as # a sample swap, so its 2025-04 brain R1_B1 is its only copy.) dedup = FALSE keeps both copies, for # the analyses that use the replicates as replicates (bridge check, replicate floor, benchmark). aav_meta <- function(tissue, dedup = TRUE) { m <- meta[meta$tissue == tissue & meta$arm == "AAV", , drop = FALSE] if (!dedup) return(m) dup <- m |> rownames_to_column("sample") |> group_by(mouse_id) |> dplyr::filter(n() > 1, run == GFP_RUN, any(run == CRE_RUN)) |> pull(sample) m[!rownames(m) %in% dup, , drop = FALSE] } # cqn normalisation factors (genes x samples, geometric mean 1 per gene) for a count matrix cqn_nf <- function(cts) { gi <- match(rownames(cts), gene_gcl$GeneID) cq <- cqn::cqn(cts, x = gene_gcl$gc[gi], lengths = gene_gcl$length[gi], sizeFactors = colSums(cts), verbose = FALSE) nf <- exp(cq$glm.offset) nf / exp(rowMeans(log(nf))) } # apply NORMALIZATION to a DESeqDataSet (DESeq() then uses these factors) norm_dds <- function(dds) { if (NORMALIZATION == "cqn") { normalizationFactors(dds) <- cqn_nf(counts(dds)) dds } else estimateSizeFactors(dds) } run_coef <- function(dds) grep("^run_", resultsNames(dds), value = TRUE) # Per-gene run offset (log2 2025-10 / 2025-04): FULL correction = unshrunk MLE run log2FC from # all GFP samples of the tissue (~ sex + run). `drop` leaves 2025-10 GFP samples out (checks). gfp_meta <- function(tissue, drop = character(), dedup = TRUE) aav_meta(tissue, dedup) |> rownames_to_column("sample") |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "GFP", !sample %in% drop) |> column_to_rownames("sample") |> mutate(run = factor(run, levels = c(GFP_RUN, CRE_RUN))) |> droplevels() run_offset <- function(tissue, drop = character()) { genes <- gene_qc[[tissue]]$keep gm <- gfp_meta(tissue, drop) dg <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[genes, rownames(gm)], gm, ~ sex + run) |> norm_dds() |> DESeq(quiet = TRUE) off <- results(dg, name = run_coef(dg))$log2FoldChange set_names(replace_na(off, 0), genes) } # Normalization factors = size factors x run offset on the 2025-04 samples, rescaled so each # gene's factors have geometric mean 1 (as DESeq2 expects). offset_nf <- function(dds, offset) { base <- if (NORMALIZATION == "cqn") cqn_nf(counts(dds)) else matrix(sizeFactors(estimateSizeFactors(dds)), nrow(dds), ncol(dds), byrow = TRUE, dimnames = dimnames(dds)) old <- colData(dds)$run == GFP_RUN base[, old] <- base[, old] * 2^(-offset[rownames(dds)]) normalizationFactors(dds) <- base / exp(rowMeans(log(base))) dds } # Batch term for a set of samples: 2025-10 extraction batch (1 / 2, with 2025-04 = R1) if every # 2025-10 extraction batch contains a GFP mouse, so treatment is estimated within batch; # otherwise sequencing run only (e.g. brain after excluding B13: batch 1 has no GFP, and an # extraction-batch term would leave Cre vs GFP resting on the single batch-2 Cre mouse). design_for <- function(m) { new <- m[m$run == CRE_RUN, , drop = FALSE] ok <- all(tapply(new$treatment == "GFP", droplevels(new[[BATCH]]), any)) multi_run <- n_distinct(m$run) > 1 if (ok && n_distinct(new[[BATCH]]) > 1) ~ sex + extraction_batch + treatment else if (multi_run) ~ sex + run + treatment else ~ sex + treatment } # PRIMARY: one GLM over 2025-10 Cre, 2025-10 GFP and 2025-04 GFP. The batch term removes the run # difference completely (full correction) and propagates its uncertainty; the 2025-04 GFP # contribute to the dispersion estimates. `drop` leaves samples out (leave-one-out). fit_primary <- function(tissue, drop = character()) { m <- aav_meta(tissue) m <- m[!rownames(m) %in% drop, , drop = FALSE] |> droplevels() dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[gene_qc[[tissue]]$keep, rownames(m)], m, design_for(m)) |> norm_dds() |> DESeq(quiet = TRUE) stopifnot(COEF %in% resultsNames(dds)) dds } run_deseq <- function(tissue) { genes <- gene_qc[[tissue]]$keep offset <- run_offset(tissue) # used for the correction check and the figures only dds <- fit_primary(tissue) res <- results(dds, name = COEF, alpha = PADJ_CUT) resLFC <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = COEF, type = "apeglm", quiet = TRUE) # check 1: uncorrected run difference among GFP, then out-of-sample: each 2025-10 GFP sample # is left out of the offset estimate and compared with the corrected 2025-04 GFP gm <- gfp_meta(tissue) before <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[genes, rownames(gm)], gm, ~ sex + run) |> norm_dds() |> DESeq(quiet = TRUE) |> results(alpha = PADJ_CUT) checks <- rownames(gm)[gm$run == CRE_RUN] oos <- map(set_names(checks), \(k) { om <- gm[gm$run == GFP_RUN | rownames(gm) == k, , drop = FALSE] |> droplevels() d <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[genes, rownames(om)], om, ~ run) |> offset_nf(run_offset(tissue, drop = k)) |> DESeq(quiet = TRUE) results(d, name = run_coef(d), alpha = PADJ_CUT) }) # check 2: within-run Cre vs GFP (2025-10 only) wm <- aav_meta(tissue) |> dplyr::filter(run == CRE_RUN) |> droplevels() within <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[genes, rownames(wm)], wm, design_for(wm)) |> norm_dds() |> DESeq(quiet = TRUE) |> results(name = COEF, alpha = PADJ_CUT) # check 3: leave-one-out over the 2025-10 GFP (batch-control) mice loo <- if (length(checks) > 1) map(set_names(checks), \(k) { d <- fit_primary(tissue, drop = k) list(res = results(d, name = COEF, alpha = PADJ_CUT), lfc = lfcShrink(d, coef = COEF, type = "apeglm", quiet = TRUE)$log2FoldChange) }) else list() # display object: every AAV sample of the tissue, offset applied to 2025-04, for PCA/heatmaps am <- aav_meta(tissue) |> droplevels() dds_display <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(geneCounts[genes, rownames(am)], am, ~ 1) |> offset_nf(offset) list(dds = dds, res = res, resLFC = resLFC, offset = offset, checks = checks, design = paste(deparse(design(dds)), collapse = ""), check_before = before, check_oos = oos, within = within, loo = loo, dds_display = dds_display) } # Tutorial output table + run offset + the three checks + robust flag. de_table <- function(fit) { norm <- counts(fit$dds, normalized = TRUE) |> as_tibble(rownames = "ensemblID") loo_ok <- if (length(fit$loo)) map(fit$loo, \(l) !is.na(l$res$padj) & l$res$padj < PADJ_CUT & sign(l$res$log2FoldChange) == sign(fit$res$log2FoldChange)) |> purrr::reduce(`&`) else rep(TRUE, nrow(fit$res)) as_tibble(as.data.frame(fit$res), rownames = "ensemblID") |> mutate(log2FoldChange_shrunk = fit$resLFC$log2FoldChange, run_offset_log2 = fit$offset[ensemblID], log2FoldChange_withinrun = fit$within$log2FoldChange, padj_withinrun = fit$within$padj, loo_sig = loo_ok, direction_agrees = sign(log2FoldChange) == sign(log2FoldChange_withinrun), robust = !is.na(padj) & padj < PADJ_CUT & loo_sig & direction_agrees %in% TRUE) |> left_join(dplyr::select(id2name, ensemblID, Symbol, biotype), by = "ensemblID") |> relocate(ensemblID, Symbol, biotype) |> left_join(norm, by = "ensemblID") |> arrange(padj) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fits <- tibble(tissue = TISSUES) |> mutate(fit = map(tissue, run_deseq), de = map(fit, de_table)) pwalk(fits, \(tissue, fit, de) { stem <- file.path(OBJ_DIR, tolower(tissue)) saveRDS(fit$dds, paste0(stem, "_dds.rds")) saveRDS(fit$res, paste0(stem, "_res.rds")) saveRDS(fit$resLFC, paste0(stem, "_resLFC.rds")) write_tsv(de, file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", sprintf("%s_DE_all_genes_DESeq2.tsv", tolower(tissue)))) write_tsv(dplyr::filter(de, padj < PADJ_CUT), file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", sprintf("%s_DE_sig_genes_DESeq2.tsv", tolower(tissue)))) }) de_summary <- fits |> transmute(tissue, n_tested = map_int(de, \(d) sum(!is.na(d$padj))), n_sig = map_int(de, \(d) sum(d$padj < PADJ_CUT, na.rm = TRUE)), n_up_Cre = map_int(de, \(d) sum(d$padj < PADJ_CUT & d$log2FoldChange > 0, na.rm = TRUE)), n_down_Cre = map_int(de, \(d) sum(d$padj < PADJ_CUT & d$log2FoldChange < 0, na.rm = TRUE)), n_robust = map_int(de, \(d) sum(d$robust)), design = map_chr(fit, "design"), gfp_checks = map_chr(fit, \(f) paste(f$checks, collapse = ", ")), n_sig_withinrun = map_int(fit, \(f) sum(f$within$padj < PADJ_CUT, na.rm = TRUE)), hAPOE_log2FC = map_dbl(de, \(d) d$log2FoldChange_shrunk[d$ensemblID == HUMAN_APOE] %||% NA), hAPOE_padj = map_dbl(de, \(d) d$padj[d$ensemblID == HUMAN_APOE] %||% NA)) write_csv(de_summary, file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", "DE_summary.csv")) de_summary ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # check 1: run difference among GFP before correction, and after correction for each 2025-10 # GFP mouse left out of the offset estimate (out-of-sample: the correction has not seen it) run_check <- fits |> transmute(tissue, run_DE_genes_uncorrected = map_int(fit, \(f) sum(f$check_before$padj < PADJ_CUT, na.rm = TRUE)), genes_with_offset_over_1.5x = map_int(fit, \(f) sum(abs(f$offset) > log2(1.5))), oos = map(fit, \(f) imap(f$check_oos, \(r, k) tibble(left_out = k, run_DE_genes_after = sum(r$padj < PADJ_CUT, na.rm = TRUE))) |> bind_rows())) |> unnest(oos) write_csv(run_check, file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", "run_correction_check.csv")) run_check ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

file.path(FIG_DIR, "qc", "aligner_hisat2_vs_star"), "full", 140) p_aligner } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 2 × 5 tissue sig_hisat sig_star sig_both r_shrunk_lfc 1 Liver 0 ![](02-run-correction_files/figure-html/aligner-compare-1.png){width=643.2} ::: ::: ## Batch-correction benchmark Question: with Cre (2025-10 run) and GFP (2025-04 run) sequenced in different runs, which correction removes the run effect while keeping Cre biology? Each method is fitted on a fully run-confounded set, and graded only on samples it never saw. - **Model set**: 2025-10 Cre (10) vs 2025-04 GFP from mice sequenced only once (8; the double-run mice SAD_326 and MAD_271 are left out entirely). The 2025-04 Cre samples are not used: they were different, misgenotyped mice. - **Held-out validation**: the double-run mice (same animal in both runs = pure run effect), SAD_532 (2025-10 GFP, single run), and the 2025-10-only Cre vs GFP comparison (no run confound). Methods: - `none`: ~ sex + treatment (the run-confounded comparison). - `RUVg_HK_k`: RUVg (Risso et al. 2014) with *a priori* negative controls = mouse orthologues of the Eisenberg & Levanon (2013) human housekeeping genes; k = 1-3 factors added to the model. - `tech_cov`: per-sample technical covariate (STAR uniquely-mapped %), slope estimated within group because treatment is in the model. - `cqn`: conditional quantile normalisation of gene GC content and length (Hansen et al. 2012) as DESeq2 normalisation factors. - `cqn_RUVg_HK_1`: both. - `bridge_offset`: the full run correction estimated from the double-run mice (reference only; it uses the held-out samples, so its bridge score is circular). Scores (per tissue): - **bridge_genes_2fold**: genes differing > 2-fold between the two copies of the same mouse after correction (lower = more batch removed). - **SAD532_cre_likeness**: correlation of SAD_532's deviation from the 2025-04 GFP mean with the Cre-vs-GFP difference. SAD_532 is a GFP mouse in the Cre run, so > 0 means run effect left over. - **run_aligned_pct**: % of the method's DEGs whose direction matches the same-mouse run difference (50% = chance; 90%+ = DEGs are run). - **r_with_within_run**: Spearman of the method's Cre-vs-GFP statistic with the 2025-10-only statistic (unconfounded; higher = more of the true Cre signal kept). Both use the same Cre mice, which raises every method's value equally. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} hk_human <- read_tsv(file.path(IN_DIR, "reference", "HK_genes_Eisenberg2013.txt"), col_names = c("symbol", "refseq"), show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(symbol = str_trim(symbol)) |> pull(symbol) |> unique() hk_mouse <- babelgene::orthologs(genes = hk_human, species = "mouse", human = TRUE) |> dplyr::filter(support_n >= 3) |> pull(ensembl) |> unique() gcl_file <- file.path(IN_DIR, "mcc_results", "gene_gc_length.tsv") star_map_bm <- read_tsv(file.path(IN_DIR, "mcc_results", "star_mapping_summary.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) bench_tissue <- function(tissue) { genes <- gene_qc[[tissue]]$keep aav <- aav_meta(tissue, dedup = FALSE) |> rownames_to_column("sample") double_mice <- aav |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "GFP") |> group_by(mouse_id) |> dplyr::filter(n_distinct(run) == 2) |> pull(mouse_id) |> unique() # SAD_326's 2025-10 brain (B13) is excluded, so in brain it no longer has two runs; it is still a # double-run mouse, so its 2025-04 copy stays out of the model set double_mice <- union(double_mice, c("SAD_326", "MAD_271")) model <- aav |> dplyr::filter(!mouse_id %in% double_mice, (treatment == "Cre" & run == CRE_RUN) | (treatment == "GFP" & run == GFP_RUN)) bridges <- aav |> dplyr::filter(mouse_id %in% double_mice) |> group_by(mouse_id) |> dplyr::filter(n_distinct(run) == 2) |> ungroup() s532 <- aav |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "GFP", run == CRE_RUN, !mouse_id %in% double_mice) |> pull(sample) all_s <- unique(c(model$sample, bridges$sample, s532)) am <- aav_meta(tissue, dedup = FALSE)[all_s, , drop = FALSE] |> droplevels() am$uniq <- as.numeric(scale(star_map_bm$Uniquely_mapped_reads_pct[match(all_s, star_map_bm$sample)])) cts <- geneCounts[genes, all_s] mm <- am[model$sample, , drop = FALSE] |> droplevels() # common normalised log scale for all samples sf <- estimateSizeFactorsForMatrix(cts) Y <- log2(t(t(cts) / sf) + 1) # same-mouse run difference (2025-10 minus 2025-04), averaged over bridge mice run_diff <- bridges |> split(~ mouse_id) |> map(\(b) Y[, b$sample[b$run == CRE_RUN]] - Y[, b$sample[b$run == GFP_RUN]]) |> purrr::reduce(`+`) / n_distinct(bridges$mouse_id) # nuisance-corrected log values for ALL samples: coefficients from the model set (treatment and # sex protected), applied to every sample regress_out <- function(Z) { X <- model.matrix(~ sex + treatment, mm) D <- cbind(X, Z[model$sample, , drop = FALSE]) B <- limma::lmFit(Y[, model$sample], D)$coefficients[, colnames(Z), drop = FALSE] Y - B %*% t(Z[colnames(Y), , drop = FALSE]) } deseq <- function(m, des, nf = NULL) { d <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(cts[, rownames(m)], m, des) if (!is.null(nf)) normalizationFactors(d) <- nf[, rownames(m)] / exp(rowMeans(log(nf[, rownames(m)]))) results(DESeq(d, quiet = TRUE), name = COEF, alpha = PADJ_CUT) } ruv_W <- function(k, x = cts) { ctl <- intersect(hk_mouse, rownames(x)) W <- RUVSeq::RUVg(x, cIdx = ctl, k = k, isLog = FALSE)$W rownames(W) <- colnames(x); colnames(W) <- paste0("W_", seq_len(k)); W } methods <- list() methods$none <- list(res = deseq(mm, ~ sex + treatment), Yc = Y) for_k <- map(1:3, \(k) { W <- ruv_W(k); mw <- cbind(mm, W[rownames(mm), , drop = FALSE]) list(res = deseq(mw, reformulate(c(colnames(W), "sex", "treatment"))), Yc = regress_out(W)) }) |> set_names(paste0("RUVg_HK_", 1:3)) methods <- c(methods, for_k) Zt <- matrix(am$uniq, dimnames = list(rownames(am), "uniq")) methods$tech_cov <- list(res = deseq(mm |> mutate(uniq = am[rownames(mm), "uniq"]), ~ uniq + sex + treatment), Yc = regress_out(Zt)) if (file.exists(gcl_file)) { gcl <- read_tsv(gcl_file, show_col_types = FALSE) gi <- match(genes, gcl$GeneID) cq <- cqn::cqn(cts, x = gcl$gc[gi], lengths = gcl$length[gi], sizeFactors = colSums(cts), verbose = FALSE) nf <- exp(cq$glm.offset) Ycq <- cq$y + cq$offset methods$cqn <- list(res = deseq(mm, ~ sex + treatment, nf = nf), Yc = Ycq) W1 <- ruv_W(1) mw <- cbind(mm, W1[rownames(mm), , drop = FALSE]) Y_bak <- Y; Y <- Ycq; Yc <- regress_out(W1); Y <- Y_bak methods$cqn_RUVg_HK_1 <- list(res = deseq(mw, ~ W_1 + sex + treatment, nf = nf), Yc = Yc) } # reference: full run offset from the double-run mice (circular on the bridge score) off <- rowMeans(as.matrix(run_diff)) nf_b <- matrix(1, nrow(cts), ncol(cts), dimnames = dimnames(cts)) nf_b[, am$run == GFP_RUN] <- 2^(-off) nf_b <- t(t(nf_b) * sf) Yb <- Y; Yb[, am$run == GFP_RUN] <- Yb[, am$run == GFP_RUN] + off methods$bridge_offset <- list(res = deseq(mm, ~ sex + treatment, nf = nf_b), Yc = Yb) within <- fits$fit[[match(tissue, fits$tissue)]]$within gfp_m <- model$sample[model$treatment == "GFP"]; cre_m <- model$sample[model$treatment == "Cre"] imap(methods, \(m, nm) { r <- m$res; sig <- which(r$padj < PADJ_CUT) Yc <- m$Yc pair_genes <- bridges |> split(~ mouse_id) |> map_dbl(\(b) sum(abs(Yc[, b$sample[b$run == CRE_RUN]] - Yc[, b$sample[b$run == GFP_RUN]]) > 1)) cre_sig <- rowMeans(Yc[, cre_m]) - rowMeans(Yc[, gfp_m]) s532_dev <- if (length(s532)) Yc[, s532[1]] - rowMeans(Yc[, gfp_m]) else NA both <- intersect(rownames(r)[!is.na(r$stat)], rownames(within)[!is.na(within$stat)]) tibble(tissue = tissue, method = nm, DEGs = length(sig), run_aligned_pct = if (length(sig)) 100 * mean(sign(r$log2FoldChange[sig]) == sign(run_diff[sig])) else NA_real_, bridge_genes_2fold = mean(pair_genes), SAD532_cre_likeness = if (length(s532)) cor(s532_dev, cre_sig) else NA_real_, r_with_within_run = cor(r[both, "stat"], within[both, "stat"], method = "spearman"), n_model = nrow(mm), n_bridge_mice = n_distinct(bridges$mouse_id)) }) |> bind_rows() } benchmark_tbl <- map(TISSUES, bench_tissue) |> bind_rows() |> mutate(method = factor(method, levels = unique(method))) write_csv(benchmark_tbl, file.path(CSV_DIR, "deseq2", "batch_correction_benchmark.csv")) benchmark_tbl ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} p_bench <- benchmark_tbl |> dplyr::select(tissue, method, `Bridge genes >2-fold\n(lower = batch removed)` = bridge_genes_2fold, `SAD_532 Cre-likeness\n(0 = batch removed)` = SAD532_cre_likeness, `Agreement with 2025-10-only\n(higher = biology kept)` = r_with_within_run) |> pivot_longer(-c(tissue, method), names_to = "score", values_to = "value") |> ggplot(aes(value, method, colour = tissue)) + geom_point(size = 1.4) + facet_wrap(~ score, scales = "free_x") + scale_colour_manual(values = c(Liver = "#8C510A", Brain = "#01665E")) + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_bulk() + theme(legend.position = "top") save_plot(p_bench, file.path(FIG_DIR, "deseq2", "batch_correction_benchmark"), "full", 85) p_bench ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-run-correction_files/figure-html/batch-benchmark-1.png){width=643.2} ::: ::: ## log2FC shrinkage ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Tutorial: log2FC distribution before vs after apeglm shrinkage p_shrink <- fits |> transmute(tissue, d = map(de, \(d) d |> dplyr::select(before = log2FoldChange, after = log2FoldChange_shrunk) |> pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "shrinkage", values_to = "lfc"))) |> unnest(d) |> mutate(shrinkage = factor(shrinkage, levels = c("before", "after"))) |> ggplot(aes(lfc, colour = shrinkage)) + geom_density(linewidth = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) + facet_wrap(~ tissue) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3)) + scale_colour_manual(values = c(before = "grey50", after = "black")) + labs(x = "log2 fold change (Cre / GFP)", y = "Density", colour = "LFC shrinkage") + theme_bulk() save_plot(p_shrink, file.path(FIG_DIR, "deseq2", "before_after_shrinkage"), "full", 55) p_shrink ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](02-run-correction_files/figure-html/shrinkage-check-1.png){width=643.2} ::: :::
